As employees, apprentices earn a wage and work alongside experienced staff to gain job-specific skills.  Off the job, usually on a day-release or through 1:1 sessions with an Assessor, apprentices receive training to work towards nationally recognised qualifications.

Why work with us

We deliver a variety of Intermediate and Advanced Apprenticeships to those aged 16 and above, subject to meeting eligibility criteria.

There are 3 common levels of Apprenticeship:

  • Intermediate Level = Level 2
  • Advanced Level = Level 3
  • Higher Level = Level 4/5

Apprentices work towards:

  • An appropriate apprenticeship standard at either Level 2, Level 3 or Level 4
  • Functional Skills in English, Maths and ICT (if required) up to Level 2 standard
  • Some apprenticeship standards include a knowledge based qualification which compliments your main aim and provides you with the essential knowledge you  require to be competent in your job
  • Other qualifications or requirements as specified by the particular occupation

Some employers pay the minimum apprenticeship salary; however some apprentices earn significantly more. The key benefits of doing an apprenticeship are:

  • Earning a salary, whilst receiving training
  • Gaining an apprenticeship which is an industry recognised achievement
  • Learning skills specific to your chosen career through hands-on experience

If you are not already working, Chelmsford College will try and help match you with an employer to ensure that the role provides the training you want. If you are already in employment, then we will work with your employer to ensure that you are getting what you need out of the training.

Our programmes for learners with special educational needs centre around INSPIRE, which aim to provide additional support for those learners who may require it.

INSPIRE is made up of three pathways; each one is varied and aimed at different learners. They are as follows:

Courses for Students with Special Educational Needs

Bespoke Provision: This offers young adults with SEND a chance to develop essential life skills that can progress them onto a variety of pathways, including vocational courses, employment, and supported living.

Foundation Provision: This pathway has several courses within it, ranging from Employment to Life Skills and Independence, depending on the individual learner's aims.

Supported Internships: This is for learners who have an EHCP and wish to work.
These courses are part of our INSPIRE department and aim to provide additional support for those with special educational needs in Essex.

Our RE-START Programmes are aimed at learners who struggle with large groups and the more formal structure associated with college-wide, vocational programmes. Learners may have been homeschooled, have an EHCP, have experienced high levels of anxiety or mental health challenges and require a more relaxed learning style. They are unsure of their chosen pathway but are interested in returning to education.

RE-START features whole-year, full-time programmes (Re-Connect) for those who may have missed out on education previously but are able to undertake a full-time programme. It also features part-time programmes aimed at learners unable to manage a full-time programme (Re-Set, Award & Certificate), perfect for helping learners gradually return to education.
